claims.text: A data-driven model incorporating oxygen-related defects will predict HfNbTaTiZr conductivity more accurately than traditional analytical models.
Traditional analytical conductivity models for HfNbTaTiZr assume a perfect, defect-free crystal.
Spark plasma sintering of gas-atomized powder can produce bulk, single-phase, random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr.
HfNbTaTiZr made by spark plasma sintering of gas-atomized powder has approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The predictive framework will use oxygen-induced defects, defect energy levels, correlated scattering, and lattice distortion as input features.
Oxygen contamination in HfNbTaTiZr generates structural disorder or defect clusters.
Oxygen impurities in HfNbTaTiZr create in-gap defect energy levels.
Electrical conduction from 0 to 200 K in oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr is dominated by ionization of defect states.
Intrinsic band conduction emerges from 300 to 1200 K in oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr.
Experimental conductivity benchmarks exist in both specified temperature regimes for HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen-induced defects lower the local symmetry of HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect energy levels facilitate thermal excitation of charge carriers at low temperature.
Defect energy levels modify the activation energy governing high-temperature conduction.
Accounting for defect-mediated conduction channels and scattering will better capture non-ideal carrier dynamics in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-related defect ionization will enhance conductivity from 0 to 200 K relative to a perfect-crystal prediction.
Oxygen-related defects will shift the high-temperature activation energy and Arrhenius slope relative to a perfect-crystal prediction.
The model is applicable only to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen, at ambient pressure, over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The magnitude of prediction-error reduction is uncertain because defect distributions and oxygen-related scattering and band modifications are difficult to model.
A low-oxygen HfNbTaTiZr batch can serve as a control for a batch containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Failure to achieve statistically lower conductivity-prediction error than the perfect-crystal model in both temperature regimes would falsify the hypothesis.
